transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Um… yeah, thanks. I guess the main thing is my appetite’s been kind of off the last few weeks. It’s probably not a huge deal, but I’m noticing I’m barely hungry, and even stuff I usually like after a shift just kind of sits there. I’ll make myself take a few bites, but that’s about it. I figured I should probably get it checked out, if that makes sense.
How long has your appetite been this way — can you pinpoint when you first noticed it?

I think it’s been about three weeks now. It sort of started around when the casino reorganized our security operations and my assignments changed. I didn’t think much of it at first, but… yeah, that’s about when I noticed I wasn’t really feeling hungry like usual.
Have you noticed that you’re not getting as much pleasure out of things you usually enjoy, like hobbies or time with friends or family?

Yeah… a little, I guess. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but stuff I usually like just hasn’t been pulling me in. I used to look forward to my morning runs, playing guitar a bit, cooking dinner… lately I keep skipping those things because they just feel like chores. Like I can’t really get myself to care about them the way I normally would. Does that make sense?
Have you been feeling down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day, over these past few weeks?

Yeah… I mean, I wouldn’t say I’m, like, falling apart or anything. But most days there’s this kind of heavy, flat feeling I’m carrying around. Even when I’m home with my family or sitting in the break room, I feel like I’m there physically, but not really… there. If that makes sense.
Have you noticed any changes in your sleep, like waking up much earlier than usual and not being able to fall back asleep?

Not really… I mean, I don’t think I’ve been waking up super early like that. My sleep might be a little off here and there, but nothing I’d want to overstate. I’m not lying awake at 4 a.m. every day or anything like that.
Have you noticed that you’ve been feeling more tired or that it’s harder to get through your day, even if you’ve had enough rest?

I don’t think so, not in a big way. I mean, I get tired like anybody does after work, but I haven’t really noticed some major drop where I can’t get through the day. At least… nothing that stands out enough that I’d want to say yes to that, if that makes sense.
Have you found yourself feeling more guilty about things lately, or maybe feeling like you’re not worth much or that you’re letting people down?

I don’t think so… not really in that way. I mean, I’ll feel bad if I snap at someone or don’t do something around the house, but I don’t think I’m sitting around thinking I’m worthless or anything like that. I hope that answers it right.

Can you tell me a bit more about how you’ve been feeling about the things you used to enjoy — like your morning runs or cooking dinner — have you completely lost interest in them, or does it come and go?

Yeah… I guess it does come up there a bit. I wouldn’t say I’ve completely lost interest, exactly, but… the stuff I used to look forward to doesn’t feel the same.

Like I used to actually want to get up and go for a run in the morning, or mess around on the guitar, or cook dinner after work. Lately I keep skipping those things, and it’s not because I hate them or anything. They just feel like chores, like something I have to force myself to care about. I don’t know if that counts as losing interest, but that’s probably the best way I can explain it.
Have you noticed a significant drop in your energy levels or felt more fatigued lately, even when doing things that normally wouldn’t wear you out?

Not really, no… I wouldn’t say it’s been a significant drop. I mean, I have days where I’m kind of worn out, sure, but nothing where normal stuff suddenly feels exhausting or anything like that. At least not that I’ve really noticed. Is that the kind of thing you mean?

Have you noticed that you're having a harder time making decisions, or that your thoughts feel slowed down? Or maybe you've noticed that your physical movements feel more sluggish or delayed than usual?

Maybe a little, yeah. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but at work a couple people have mentioned I seem kind of slow getting going in briefings… like I’m taking longer to respond than I normally would.

It’s not like I can’t do my job or anything, but sometimes it feels like my body and my mouth are both a step behind everybody else. I wasn’t sure if that was the kind of thing you meant.
Would you say that you’ve completely lost interest in the things you used to enjoy, like your morning runs or cooking dinner, or does the interest come and go?

I don’t think it’s completely gone, no… it’s more like I just don’t reach for those things the way I used to.

I used to look forward to my morning runs, or playing guitar a bit, or making dinner, and lately I keep putting them off. They just feel like chores now, like something I should do but can’t quite get myself to care about. I don’t know if that’s the right way to put it.
Would you say that you’ve completely lost interest in the things you used to enjoy, like your morning runs or cooking dinner, or does the interest come and go?

Yeah… I think it comes and goes, but mostly I just haven’t been doing them. Like, I used to actually look forward to my morning runs, playing guitar, cooking dinner, that kind of thing.

Lately I keep skipping them, or putting them off, because they feel more like chores than anything I want to do. It’s not that I hate them or anything… I just can’t really get myself to care about them the way I used to, if that makes sense.
Would you say that most days, for the past few weeks, you’ve been feeling down or depressed for most of the day?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I wouldn’t want to make it sound dramatic, but most days there’s this kind of heavy, flat feeling I’m carrying around.

Even when I’m at home with my family, or just sitting in the break room at work, I’m there, but I don’t really feel there, if that makes sense. It’s been like that a lot lately.
Would you say that you’ve lost interest in almost everything you used to enjoy, to the point where nothing really feels rewarding or satisfying anymore?

I don’t know if I’d say almost everything… maybe that sounds too strong. But the main things I used to enjoy, yeah, they don’t really feel the same.

Like my morning runs, playing guitar, cooking dinner… I used to look forward to those. Lately I just keep skipping them or putting them off, because they feel more like chores. It’s not that I think they’re awful, I just can’t really get myself to care about them the way I used to. Does that make sense?
Would you say that you’ve lost interest in almost all activities you used to enjoy, to the point where very few things, if any, feel rewarding or satisfying anymore?

Yeah… I guess I’d say it’s close to that, though I don’t want to overstate it.

The main things I used to look forward to—my morning runs, playing guitar, cooking dinner—I keep skipping them now. They just feel like chores, like something I’m supposed to do, not something I actually want to do. I can’t really get myself to care about them the way I used to.

I don’t know if that answers it right, but… yeah, very few things feel that satisfying lately.

Completely… I don’t know if I’d say completely. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is.

But yeah, the things I used to look forward to—like running in the mornings, playing guitar, cooking dinner—I’ve been skipping them a lot. They just feel like chores now, like something I should do, and I can’t really get myself to care about them much.

So… not nothing at all, maybe, but it’s pretty close to feeling like not much is rewarding. Does that make sense?

I’m not sure I’d say completely… I don’t want to make it sound more dramatic than it is.

But yeah, the stuff I used to actually look forward to—my morning runs, playing guitar, making dinner—I’ve been skipping a lot of it lately. It just feels like another chore, and I can’t really get myself to care about it the way I used to.

So… maybe not nothing feels rewarding, but it’s definitely a lot less than before. Is that what you mean?

I mean… I don’t know if “completely” is the right word. I don’t want to exaggerate.
